title.value: A Cross-Domain Transferable Neural Coherence Model
title.justification: The provided title of the paper as mentioned at the beginning of the provided text.
title.quote: A Cross-Domain Transferable Neural Coherence Model

analysis.description: The paper introduces a local discriminative neural model for coherence modeling which addresses limitations of existing coherence models by efficiently learning against incorrect sentence orderings. It demonstrates superior performance in sentence coherence across domains using a Wall Street Journal dataset and new challenging Wikipedia categories.

type.justification: The paper presents an empirical study by conducting experiments to demonstrate the model's performance across various datasets and evaluating its effectiveness in coherence modeling.
type.quote: We demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach on the Wall Street Journal (WSJ) benchmark dataset, as well as on three challenging new evaluation protocols using different categories of articles drawn from Wikipedia that contain increasing levels of domain diversity.

name.justification: The research focuses on modeling text coherence, an important aspect of NLP concerning the logical and semantic organization of text.
name.quote: Coherence is an important aspect of text quality and is crucial for ensuring its readability... The standard task used to test a coherence model in NLP is sentence ordering.

name.justification: The paper mainly addresses the issue of coherence in texts for various NLP applications, focusing on sentence ordering and cross-domain coherence.
name.quote: Coherence is an important aspect of text quality and is crucial for ensuring its readability.

name.justification: The paper implements a neural model that integrates previous generative and discriminative approaches, a core aspect of machine learning methodologies.
name.quote: Our method relies on two key ideas. The first is to reexamine the operating assumption of previous work that a global, passage-level model is necessary for good performance.

name.justification: The paper introduces a local discriminative neural model (LCD) as a novel contribution to coherence modeling.
name.quote: We propose the local coherence discriminator model (LCD) whose operating assumption is that the global coherence of a document can be well approximated by the average of coherence scores between consecutive pairs of sentences.

is_contributed.justification: The model is proposed by the authors as a new approach.
is_contributed.quote: Our contributions are: 1. We correct the misconception that discriminative models cannot generalize well for cross-domain coherence scoring, with a novel local discriminative neural model.

is_executed.justification: The paper reports experimental results which imply execution of the model.
is_executed.quote: Experimental results on a wide range of tasks and datasets demonstrate that the proposed model outperforms previous state-of-the-art methods significantly and consistently on both domain-specific and open-domain datasets.

is_compared.justification: The paper compares the new model with several baselines to demonstrate its effectiveness.
is_compared.quote: Our proposed models perform significantly better than all other baselines, even if we use the most naïve sentence encoder, i.e., averaged GloVe vectors.
